label: letter s input at original position >= 3 (after h/i/b/u/m/j/d/y earlier)
explanation: Fires only on input token s during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It never fires on any other token, on <DEL>, or in the copy phase, and almost never before position 3: t=2 gives only tiny activations and t=0-1 none. The firing rate on s goes up with position (orig_idx 3: 0.8%, 4-8: about 1.3-1.6% of all steps) and is higher on the first occurrence of s (90% of mass). Whether a given s fires depends on the earlier prefix. Sequences that contain h, i, b, u, m, j, d or y before the s fire much more often, and the top activations are all s after prefixes like h h d 0 y or b i h 0 0 m k. The bare rule s at t>=3 catches about 100% of the mass but only 38% of those steps are active (dev F1 0.55). Adding the condition that one of those letters appeared earlier raises precision to 0.48 and keeps 98% of the mass (dev F1 0.64). The rest of the prefix dependence looks distributed, and no simple token set captured it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: s, -, <DEL>, f, 3, c; least: o, w, z, 0) and the first original token (most: i, b, h, u, m, j; least: n, x, c, z); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
